title: Outreach sequences
description: Three-round email drafts per tier. Written against the do_not_claim list in gtm.json: no claim that escort prevents attack, no current pricing, no assertion that any recipient buys escort today. Variables in double braces are filled per account.

cadence.then: mark dead or move to quarterly

compliance_note: Most tier 1 and 2 targets are EU or UK entities. Business-to-business outreach to a corporate address is generally permitted, but include a real sender identity, a postal address and a one-click opt-out, and honour opt-outs immediately. Check current GDPR and PECR position before the first send.

sequences.channel: LinkedIn message from the founder, not email
sequences.premise: A first-degree connection routes around the two things blocking us: eight of sixteen companies publish no named leadership, and four of the attacked companies have no website. Ask for their judgment, not for a meeting about our product. It is a far easier yes and it gets us the truth.
sequences.length_rule: Three or four lines. A LinkedIn message is not an email.

rounds.variant: the buyer — someone who holds DPA, CSO or fleet
rounds.subject: (LinkedIn message, no subject)
rounds.body:
{{first_name}} — We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.

You have sat in the {{their_role}} seat, so you know better than I do whether a manager would ever put one alongside a hull.

Twenty minutes to tell me where it falls down?

rounds.variant: the route-in — commercial, agency or broker side
rounds.subject: (LinkedIn message, no subject)
rounds.body:
{{first_name}} — We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.

{{their_patch}} is exactly your patch. Two things I would value more than a market report: have you seen anyone actually buy protection like this, and who at your customers makes that call?

Twenty minutes?

rounds.variant: mutual connection — ask for the introduction first
rounds.subject: (message to the mutual, not the target)
rounds.body:
{{mutual_name}} — you know {{target_name}} at {{target_company}}. We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages.

{{target_first_name}} sits close to the decision we need to understand. Worth an introduction, or would you rather I approach directly?

sequences.premise: They hold the ISM Document of Compliance and make the operational call. They manage hundreds of hulls, so the conversation scales.

rounds.subject: Autonomous escort for commercial ships
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.

{{company}} manages around {{fleet}} hulls. Every one that goes through the southern Red Sea is a decision that lands on your desk, not the owner's.

If any of them are still making that transit, we can escort them.

Thursday or Friday?

{{sender}}

rounds.subject: Re: Escort cover across the {{company}} managed fleet
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

One follow-up, with the number that made us take this seriously.

There were 38 reported attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, the fewest since 1992. But 84% of them ended with the ship boarded or hijacked, and 67 seafarers were taken. Fewer attacks, higher consequence each time.

If protection is not your desk, just point me at the right one.

Still happy to walk you through the record. Early next week?

{{sender}}

rounds.subject: Last note
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

Last note from me.

We keep a sourced record of every reported attack, who actually owns and manages the ships that were hit, and what each platform in this market can really do. It is yours if it is useful, with nothing attached.

{{sender}}

sequences.premise: They have already absorbed the loss. The need does not need arguing, so the email should be short and specific to their vessel.
sequences.warning: Crew were killed on True Confidence and taken hostage on Eternity C and Abdullah. The incident is referenced once, after the introduction, and never as the opening line. A human reads every tier 2 send before it goes.

rounds.subject: Autonomous escort for commercial ships
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.

{{vessel}} is why you are on a very short list. Most owners have read about these attacks. You have had one.

If {{company}} still has ships on that route, we can escort them.

rounds.subject: Re: Marine security, autonomous escort vessels
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

One more, and it is the part that argues against us.

An escort is not a guarantee. The Maersk Yorktown was fired on under a two-destroyer escort. About half the successful attacks in the first half of 2026 were on ships at anchor, where an escort does nothing.

We think the case is strongest against drones and small boats on a moving hull in a defined passage, and weakest at anchor. Whether that narrow case is worth paying for is your call, not ours.

The offer stands: twenty minutes, and you get the incident record regardless. Early next week?

{{sender}}

Twenty minutes and the route data is yours. Early next week?

sequences.premise: Five named incidents in the library involve tankers. High hull value, so the war risk premium bites hardest.

rounds.body:

We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.

Tankers carry the highest hull values through the worst water. The Red Sea attacks have been drone and missile led, and a hull your size is the target that justifies the missile.

If your tankers are still making that passage, we can escort them.

rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

One more, with the honest caveat attached.

The only published escort pricing we can find is from 2012: a convoy escort operation charged roughly $30,000 for one boat covering about four vessels for three to four days. That works out near $7,500 a vessel against $50,000 to $60,000 for an embarked armed team. Those are old numbers and the per-vessel split is our arithmetic, not a published finding.

Which is exactly why we want a current view from an owner rather than another report.

Which is exactly why I want a current read from an owner rather than another report. Early next week?

sequences.premise: On voyage, time and bareboat charters the charterer usually bears the war risk premium. Structurally the best-motivated buyer, and the one we know least about.

If you can tell me we are wrong, that is worth the email.

If you can tell me we are wrong about that, it is worth the twenty minutes. Early next week?

sequences.premise: Everyone else in this file is sold protection. An underwriter is not buying protection — they are buying the ability to write business they are currently declining or excluding. So the opening line is about their premium income, not their safety. In 2026 the market repriced and excluded whole geographies rather than withdrawing: Hormuz went from 0.1% of hull value to 7.5-10%, and the southern Red Sea and Saudi-linked tonnage were carved out entirely. Every one of those exclusions is premium an underwriter would rather have written.
sequences.length_rule: Very short. Opening line, one qualifying line, one question, sign off. An underwriter reading a cold email at 8am will not reach paragraph four. Never longer than six lines.
sequences.warning: Do NOT state or imply that carrying an escort will reduce a premium, earn a rating credit, or is recognised by any underwriter. Nobody has told us that it does — it is the single largest open question in our own library, and asserting it would be an unverifiable claim made to the one audience qualified to catch it. The whole sequence asks the question rather than answering it. A human reads every tier 6 send before it goes.

rounds.variant: underwriting — CUO, head of marine, war-risk underwriter
rounds.subject: Autonomous escort — does it change what you can quote?
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

I have an autonomous vessel that can help you write more premium. It reduces the risk from drones and small boats against a moving hull in a defined passage.

That is the whole pitch. The part I cannot answer is yours: does a verified escort change what you are willing to quote in a listed area, or is it worth nothing at the desk?

Fifteen minutes?

{{sender}}

rounds.subject: Re: autonomous escort
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

One more, and it is the part that argues against us.

An escort is not a guarantee. The Maersk Yorktown was fired on under a two-destroyer escort, and roughly half the successful attacks in the first half of 2026 were on ships at anchor, where an escort does nothing.

So the honest claim is narrow: drones and small boats, moving hull, defined passage. If that narrow claim is still worth something to you, there is a conversation.

{{sender}}

rounds.subject: Closing the file?
rounds.body:
{{first_name}},

Last one.

If a verified escort is not something you would ever rate for, say so and I will close the file. That answer is genuinely useful to us — we would rather know than keep guessing.

If it might be, I will send operating data rather than a deck.

{{sender}}

why_this_tier_is_different: The other tiers sell risk reduction to the party that bears the loss. This one sells capacity to the party that bears the risk of writing it.

The 2026 pattern is exclusion, not withdrawal. The LMA's own March 2026 survey found 88% of Lloyd's marine war participants still writing hull war and over 90% still writing cargo — the market repriced and carved out geographies. Every carve-out is unwritten premium.

The decision may not sit with the insurer at all. Both 2026 cancellations were served on the clubs BY their reinsurers. Gard's Circular 01/2026 says so in its opening sentence. Where a contact holds a reinsurance brief, that is the more important conversation.
Pair the two round-1 variants at the same organisation. Loss prevention certifies that a measure works; underwriting decides whether that is worth anything. Neither can answer alone.

alternates.use_when: The contact's role_class is insurer-loss-prevention, or their title contains 'loss prevention' or 'risk engineer'.
alternates.why: Loss prevention does not price anything, so asking them what they would quote is the wrong question. They are the seat that decides whether a measure demonstrably works, which is the gate before pricing. Fifteen of the tier 6 contacts sit in this role class.
alternates.how_to_run: Do NOT add this as a second round 1 — the engine resolves a round by number and would silently ignore it, and the cadence timeline would draw two nodes on day 0. Run it as a campaign instead: the Campaign schema in server/src/outreach/schemas.ts exists for exactly this, a persona and message aimed at a chosen set of accounts independent of their tier. Set template_tier 6 and select the loss-prevention contacts.
alternates.subject: What evidence would you need?
alternates.body:
{{first_name}},

I have an autonomous vessel that can help you write more premium. It reduces the risk from drones and small boats against a moving hull in a defined passage.

You are the person who would have to be satisfied it actually reduces risk before anyone prices it differently. So I would rather ask what evidence you would need than send you a deck.

Fifteen minutes?

{{sender}}

gaps: No sequence has been sent or tested. Reply rates are unknown.
No sender identity, postal address or opt-out mechanism is configured yet.
Tier 2 drafts reference vessels on which crew were killed or taken. Have a human read every one before it sends.
The drafts now lead with the site's own positioning. None has been reviewed by whoever owns the brand voice.

positioning.source: Taken from seaworth.ai, not written for this sequence.
positioning.site_line: Our vessels escort commercial ships through high-risk passages, protecting them from piracy and drone attacks.
positioning.site_stance: We allow commercial ships to pass through. We are not associated with any military, nor do we sell to military organizations.
positioning.standard_intro: We build autonomous vessels that escort commercial ships through high-risk passages and protect them from piracy and drone attacks.
positioning.rule: Every round 1 opens with this introduction verbatim, before saying why we are writing to that company.
corrections: Earlier drafts described the product only against piracy and boarding. The site names drone and aerial threats first-class, and the Houthi campaign is drone and missile based, so the drafts were understating the product.
Earlier drafts omitted the commercial-only stance. It is a deliberate position on the site and a genuine differentiator: 45 of the 123 companies in market-players.json are military-only.

First version read as a corporate boilerplate: 'We provide Marine Security as a Service:', a legalistic military disclaimer and a line about being in stealth. Replaced with the mission in one sentence.
Removed 'Commercial operators only. We do not work with navies.' from the body. The constraint is enforced by who is on the list, not by a disclaimer in the email.
Cut 'I am writing to you because' from every round 1 and removed 'modelled'. Both are stock cold-email tells: the first announces the email rather than giving the reason, the second is desk language.
Round 1 close was apologetic and asked three open questions, which invites a reply instead of a meeting. Replaced with a concrete offer of the research plus a two-day close.
Round 1 was offering free research instead of selling escort, and undercut the product in the pitch paragraph. Rewritten to make the offer: first operators, one route, one ship.
Replaced the 'selecting the first operators' offer with a plain one: if you have ships on that route, we can escort them.
Cut 'If you would rather not, say so and I will leave it' from the tier 2 close. It handed them the exit before they reached the ask. The close is two words: Thursday or Friday?
voice: State the mission, then the reason for writing, then one ask. Never announce that you are writing.
Lead the second paragraph with the fact itself, not with why it is being mentioned.
Say the honest limitation before they have to ask for it.
Never more than about 150 words in round 1.
positioning.scope_note: We sell to commercial entities only. That is a targeting rule, not a line in the email: the account list is filtered to commercial operators, so stating it in the copy is redundant and reads defensively.
banned: I am writing to you / I am reaching out / I wanted to reach out — announcing the email instead of giving the reason.
as a Service, solutions, leading provider, best-in-class, cutting-edge
I hope this finds you well
Just following up / circling back / touching base
synergy, leverage, partner with you on
book a call / book time / grab 15 minutes
let me know if you are interested
We are early (as an opener — apologising for yourself)
offering to 'bring what we hold' or share research in round 1
hedging the product in the same paragraph that pitches it
selecting the first operators / first cohort / limited slots — invented scarcity
If you would rather not… / no pressure / apologies for the intrusion — offering the exit inside the ask

close.rule: Round 1 and 2 close by offering something they keep, then naming two days. Never say 'book a call', 'book time', 'grab 15 minutes' or 'let me know if you are interested'.
close.why: The asset is real: a sourced attack record, the ownership chains and a 39-platform comparison. Leading with what they get makes the meeting worth taking even if they never buy.

selling.rule: Round 1 offers the service in one plain sentence: if you have ships on that route, we can escort them.
selling.structure: [what we do] + [why this company, one specific fact] + [the offer, one sentence] + [two days]
rejected: Offering to bring our research. Gives away the asset and makes us sound like consultants.
'We are selecting the first operators we escort.' Fake scarcity, and awkward.
'One route, one ship, and you see what it does.' Hedging the offer while making it.
selling.hedging: The honest limitation stays in round 2. It does not belong in the opening pitch.

positioning.warm_rule: Where a target is a first-degree connection, it is a short LinkedIn message from the founder asking for their judgment. Never the cold email sequence. Where a mutual connection exists, ask for the introduction before messaging directly.

open_question_for_founder: Round 1 now states flatly: 'we can escort them'. That is a capability claim and nothing in this library backs it. Before any send, confirm what we can actually commit to today — a live escorted transit, a paid pilot, or a design-partner conversation — because a ship manager may say yes on Thursday.
